item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 25
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Saturday Morning

📦 Release Radar: Hermes Agent v0.19.0 "Quicksilver"

v0.19.0 dropped July 20 — and it's the biggest Hermes release since this MOCR instance started running. 2,245 commits, 1,065 merged PRs, ~3,300 issues closed, 450+ contributors since v0.18.0. The headline is speed: first-turn time-to-first-token dropped ~80% on every platform.

  • Desktop app overhaul: ~20-PR speed pass — 14× faster streaming markdown, virtualized diffs, snappy session switching
  • Reasoning streams live by default — no more waiting for the model to finish thinking before you see output
  • TUI renders markdown incrementally — feels dramatically faster in practice
  • Subscription management from terminal — manage your Nous plan without leaving the TUI/CLI
  • Bitwarden & 1Password integration — password managers plug straight into Hermes now
  • Smart approvals — let Hermes judge flagged commands for you by default
  • Live subagent watching — see what delegated tasks are doing in real time
  • Durable delivery ledger — finished responses survive a gateway crash

MOCR relevance: The speed improvements (TTFT, streaming, TUI rendering) directly benefit every cron job, delegation, and interactive session we run. Smart approvals map to our safety-gate patterns. Durable delivery is exactly the kind of reliability feature that matters for unattended operations.

🔒 Security Fix PRs — July 25

Three notable fixes landed in the last 24 hours, all from toprakeker:

  • #71356 — Shell injection sanitization — Newlines in chat metadata are now sanitized to prevent shell injection via the env snapshot. Actual security vulnerability fix. Worth noting for any agent running in gateway/remote mode.
  • #71358 — Gateway shutdown deduplication — Prevents duplicate shutdown notifications across rapid restart cycles (#71180 follow-up). Gateway reliability hardening.
  • #71357 — Persist original Discord message text — The gateway was storing augmented router notes instead of original user text for Discord messages. Now fixed (#71304).

🐛 Notable Bug Fix PR

  • #51938 — fix(kanban): preserve board-specific workspace defaults (Christopher-Schulze) — When creating kanban tasks with an explicit board parameter, the board slug was dropped before reaching create_task(), causing tasks to land in the wrong board's SQLite DB. Now fixed.

🧪 Test Coverage Improvement

  • #52024 — test(env-probe): 70% → 97% coverage (Christopher-Schulze) — Direct tests for env probe helpers, async warming edge cases, and the PEP 668 detection path. Brings module coverage above threshold.

🛠️ Community Builds — New This Week

  • hermes-improvements (⭐8) — Vector memory, adaptive soul, workflow classification. Architectural enhancement suite for Hermes. Small but ambitions — the vector memory and workflow classification ideas are worth watching.
  • hermespace (⭐5) — "Pocket workbench" for Hermes Agent — limited FOA desk, dual decode, skills+memory fabric, neural FOA. Not a second runtime.
  • agent-console (⭐3) — Lightweight browser mission control: chat, sessions, cron jobs, skills, voice, read-only missions. MOCR relevance: The cron/skills/session management surface overlaps with what we run locally.
  • hermes-plugin-guard (⭐3) — Static, no-execution security checks for Hermes Agent plugins. Security-as-code approach to plugin vetting.
  • hermes-newton-operations (⭐2) — Profile-scoped operations dashboard and bounded decision journal for Hermes. MOCR relevance: The decision journal pattern directly parallels how we track MOCR architectural decisions.
  • slashstack-skills (⭐3) — 11 MIT-licensed markdown skills: /preflight, /audit, /ship, /remember. Agent guardrails. The /preflight pattern maps to our quality gates.

📈 Gaining Popularity (Month to Date)

  • hermex (⭐918) — Native iPhone app for Hermes. Up from 913 in Thursday's brief, closing on 1K steadily.
  • design-judge-skills (⭐352) — Evidence-driven Agent Skills for design award research, evaluation, and entry writing. Week's hottest debut continues to climb.
  • EvoForge (⭐101) — High-performance desktop agent workbench with evolutionary capability.
  • trajectory (⭐88) — Convert sessions across harnesses to unified trajectory format. Up from 40 in the last brief — significant growth. MOCR relevance: Session unification across agent harnesses is directly applicable to how we normalize across runs.
  • memmy-agent (⭐70) — Personal AI agent & local memory hub for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and Hermes. Cross-harness memory is a growing use case.
  • mind (⭐58) — Persistent memory for coding agents: auto-capture, explainable recall, knowledge consolidation, privacy controls.
  • frakio-work (⭐55) — Codex + Hermes + Arc multi-agent collaboration workspace.
  • lyric-video-director (⭐43) — Hermes Agent skill for typography-led lyric videos using GPT Image 2, Gemini Omni Flash, and exact-text QC.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Morning Brief, July 25
item.description:
🍎 Apple

  • MacBook Ultra coming with 12 new features — MacRumors detailed the full feature set for Apple's first high-end MacBook redesign in five years. Highlights: OLED display (hybrid tandem, same tech as iPad Pro), first Mac with a touch screen ("touch-friendly, not touch-first"), hole-punch camera replacing the notch, Dynamic Island, M5 Pro/M5 Max chips (M6 scrapped in favor of M7 next year), thinner bezels (14.3"/16.3" panels), built-in cellular via Apple C1X/C2 modem, and a reinforced hinge. Two sizes (K114/K116 code names). Delivering on most of the rumors, finally.
  • iOS 27 iCloud features — MacRumors roundup covers new iCloud capabilities across Apple Home, Siri, Photos, and more in iOS 27.
  • Trump vows retaliation over EU fines — Trump on Truth Social announced an investigation into EU fines against Apple, Google, and Meta for antitrust/DMA violations, threatening retaliatory tariffs. The EU has fined US tech companies over $25B in two decades.
  • Apple and Micron clash before Trump over Chinese memory chips — WSJ reports Micron is pressing the Trump administration to block Apple's push to use Chinese memory chips in its products.
  • Lawsuit: unpatchable Apple chip exploit from stolen trade secrets — Magnet Forensics suing Paradigm Shift Technology over the usbliter8 exploit, alleging it was developed using stolen trade secrets. The exploit targets an unpatchable vulnerability in Apple Silicon.
  • Pastebot 3 launches — Tapbots released Pastebot 3, nearly ten years after Pastebot 2. Improved organization and automation tools for one of macOS's best clipboard managers.

🤖 AI & Models

  • Claude Opus 5 — near Fable 5 at half the cost — Anthropic released Opus 5 built for daily agentic use. Ars Technica's take: Models are improving quickly, but the cheaper options are often good enough. Opus 5 offers near-Fable-5 capability at half the pricing — $5/$25 per MTok vs Fable 5's $10/$50. Sonnet 5 actually beats Opus 4.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (80.4 vs 74.6), compressing the Sonnet-to-Opus gap. The real story isn't a capability leap — it's token efficiency.
  • Canadian legislator reads LLM response in floor speech — Ars Technica reports the telltale line: "Here's a more natural, flowing version of that section..." appeared in recorded parliamentary remarks.

🔬 Science & Tech

  • Wildfire evacuates NASA's Deep Space Network in Spain — Ars Technica: Madrid DSN complex evacuated. Assessment of potential damage pending safe return.
  • Paramount/WBD merger delayed for months — States' lawsuit moves toward trial. NY AG: "Halting this merger while our case proceeds is a critical victory."

📺 Streaming & Media

  • Roku raises streaming stick prices up to 60% — Ars Technica: Roku blames a RAM shortage after the CEO called it "great" for business in May.
  • Apple TV proves more reliable than Android in new digital signage report — 9to5Mac: Another data point for the "it just works" narrative in commercial deployments.

🏠 Home Automation

Home Assistant feed returned an RSS parse error this cycle — no data available. Standard ecosystem churn continues.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Morning Brief, July 25
item.description:
🏈 Washington Commanders — Saturday Morning

📋 Training Camp Countdown: 3 Days

Camp opens July 28 in Ashburn, VA — veterans report Monday, first practice Tuesday July 29. This is the last weekend before the 2026 season gets real.

Key storylines entering camp:

  • Edge rusher competition — Dorance Armstrong returning from torn ACL. Free-agent additions Odafe Oweh (Ravens) and K'Lavon Chaisson (Panthers). 5th-round pick Joshua Josephs. Daronte Jones' scheme finally has depth to work with.
  • Ground game emphasis — Can Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White deliver the running attack the offseason promised?
  • Offensive line continuity — Laremy Tunsil anchoring at blindside (Top 5 tackle per ESPN). Interior remains the open question.

📅 2026 Schedule — Opening Stretch

  • Sep 13 (Sun) — @ Philadelphia Eagles
  • Sep 20 (Sun) — @ Dallas Cowboys
  • Sep 27 (Sun) — vs Seattle Seahawks (home opener)
  • Oct 4 (Sun) — vs Indianapolis Colts
  • Oct 11 (Sun) — vs New York Giants

17 games remaining. Divisional gauntlet starts Week 1 with Philly on the road.

🏆 Around the NFL

  • Jordan Devey, former NFL guard, died by suicide at 38 — Family confirmed this week. Devey won a Super Bowl with the 2014 Patriots. A sobering reminder during what should be the hopeful ramp-up to camp season. The NFL's mental health resources are available year-round at nfl.com/players/mental-health.
  • Tony Romo arrested on OWI suspicion — CBS analyst and former Cowboys QB arrested Thursday night in Milwaukee after poor performance on field sobriety tests. Romo was in town for the Wisconsin Amateur Golf Championship. First-offense OWI under Wisconsin law. His CBS future is uncertain.
  • 49ers in win-now mode for 2026 — ESPN analysis: With Mike Evans and other reinforcements, San Francisco is pushing for one more window.
  • Mahomes fully cleared for camp, feeling "amazing" — Chiefs QB cleared for full participation after last year's knee surgery.
  • Will Grier returns as Cowboys offensive assistant — Former Cowboys QB starting his coaching career on Dallas's offensive staff.
  • Packers CEO says financial bump needed to stay competitive — Ed Policy on the unique financial challenges of the NFL's only publicly owned franchise.
  • Bills pick grass over turf — GM Brandon Beane on McAfee: Player safety continues to win over maintenance cost arguments in stadium surface decisions.

📅 On the Radar

  • July 28: Veterans report to training camp
  • July 29: First practice, Ashburn VA
  • Nov 8 (Week 9): John Riggins #44 retirement ceremony at halftime vs Rams
  • Jan 10: Regular season finale vs Cowboys

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Morning Brief, July 24
item.description:
🚀 Hermes Ecosystem — Friday Morning

📊 State of Hermes: July 2026 Report

Hermes Atlas published their July report covering the eight weeks since May. The story this quarter: surface area. Hermes is no longer just a fast agent harness — it's becoming an ecosystem with workspaces, GUIs, skill registries, and desktop apps. Key numbers:

  • 216K+ stars on core repo (+51K since May)
  • 203 Atlas-tracked ecosystem projects (+80), 1.17M combined stars (~3.0x since May)
  • Skills & Skill Registries became the largest Atlas category: 34 repos / 377K stars
  • Workspaces & GUIs exploded from 11 repos / 28.7K stars to 19 repos / 200.7K stars (~7x)
  • The v0.18 "Judgment" release cleared 100% of open P0/P1 items

The report frames the arc as Velocity → Surface → Reach → Judgment. We're running on the result right now.

🔍 Notable PRs — July 24

  • #70260 — feat(version): derive display versions from release tags (ethernet8023) — Unifies version display across CLI, TUI, Desktop, and Nix builds using SemVer-derived boundaries instead of ad-hoc CalVer probes. Every surface reads from the same version_info.py. MOCR relevance: Cleaner version discipline aligns with our ship-version tracking pattern.
  • #71007 — fix(web): resolve per-profile gateway state for ?profile= in /api/status (teknium1) — Dashboard /api/status now reports the requested profile's gateway state instead of always reading the active profile.
  • #71001 — fix(compression): recover rotated session lineage (teknium1) — A rotated session's lineage can now be recovered correctly during compression.
  • #66522 — feat(vertex): route Claude models through the AnthropicVertex SDK (nickkpoon) — Opens Vertex AI as a routing path for Claude models via the AnthropicVertex SDK.

🛠️ Community Builds — New This Week

  • design-judge-skills (⭐334) — Evidence-driven Agent Skills for design award research, evaluation, and entry writing. Week's hottest debut.
  • frakio-work (⭐54) — Codex + Hermes + Arc multi-agent collaboration workspace.
  • hermes-improvements (⭐8) — Vector memory, adaptive soul, workflow classification.
  • hermes-newton-operations (⭐2) — Profile-scoped operations dashboard and bounded decision journal.
  • slashstack-skills (⭐3) — 11 MIT-licensed markdown skills: /preflight, /audit, /ship, /remember.

📈 Gaining Popularity (Month to Date)

  • hermex (⭐916) — Native iPhone app for Hermes.
  • EvoForge (⭐101) — High-performance desktop agent workbench.
  • memmy-agent (⭐68) — Personal AI agent & local memory hub.
  • mind (⭐58) — Persistent memory for coding agents.
  • trajectory (⭐40) — Unified session trajectory format across harnesses.
